title: Binding registry for DID/NDI V_eta
description: Three coordinated registries, one per binding shape: subject_statement_bindings (keyed by variable, for statement leaves), relation_bindings (keyed by relation term, for edges), and entity_field_bindings (keyed by class+field, for a controlled-term field named directly on an entity -- e.g. an entity's `type`). subject_statement_bindings map a statement's variable (and, on interactions, method) to the statement class that carries it (its direction: assertion, observation, manipulation or calculation, with the value kind it takes; T3 since 2026-10-08). A term-valued row additionally pins the admissible term set as an enumerated values list (each an ontology term) or an ontology subtree (ontology + root_node). Rows flagged subject_defining are the kind-defining variables (D9). relation_bindings map a relation term to its carrier class (directed_relation, with child -> parent endpoints, / undirected_relation, with a symmetric member set) and the admissible endpoint entity types. Every relation name and entity type has a node (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [vocabulary nodes]); code matches a relation or an entity type by its node. Consumer tooling resolves a value or endpoint against the matching binding at validation time. unit_bindings (Jess Haley, 2026-10-29 [allowed units are source units], did_v2_go_forward_class_audit.md): one row per variable node, `{variable, source_units}`: the closed list of units a SOURCE may give that variable's value in (the value's `source_unit`), each converted to the value class's canonical unit. Seeded with time and spatial position ([allowed units are closed source_unit lists]); condition variables in use are added as they are decided. Checked by tools/check_term_registry.py R15; enforcement is DID-matlab's.

openMINDS.notes: openMINDS controlled-term instance libraries; each term_set is a flat instance library (IRI + label), not an ontology subtree. `version` is UNRESOLVED: no import path stamps a release yet.

notes: subject_statement_bindings are keyed on the variable (+ method on interactions) and name the statement class that carries it: its direction (assertion, observation, manipulation, calculation; a list where more than one is allowed) and `value_kind`. There is no separately-named value_set. Only a term-valued row carries an admissible-set spec (values or ontology+root_node); a dimensional row needs none. Rows flagged subject_defining make the subject-kind ingestion invariant precise: a subject is expected to carry >=1 term assertion whose variable matches a subject_defining binding (checked at ingest). relation_bindings enumerate the admissible relation terms (D6): the value carried on directed_relation.relation / undirected_relation.relation is a member of this set. class pins the term to its carrier and thus its endpoint symmetry: a directed_relation carries child_types -> parent_types (matching the schema child/parent deps), an undirected_relation carries a symmetric member_types (matching its single entities dep). Endpoint types may be entity, statement or value classes (#73 items 22, 27). The abstract type `entity` means 'any entity'; [] = unconstrained. The undirected rows (paired_with, same_as; #73 audit 2 D5) carry member_types. directed_relation.relation and undirected_relation.relation declare a binding whose values are GENERATED from these rows at build time, so the field and the registry cannot disagree. A relation `node` is its ontology term (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [vocabulary nodes]; "" only where no node is decided). ordered marks terms where the membership's `order` field is meaningful (T20); timed marks event edges that may carry a method/time anchor. A `clock_alignment` row binds clock_alignment.relation (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [clock alignment relation bound]): the one kind did2.convert.resolveClockAlignment's bodies write, passing nothing. A subject_statement_bindings row may name more than one subtree: `ontology` + `root_node`, plus `additional_roots` [{ontology, root_node}].

documentation: Every relation_bindings row declares `passes`, what reaches the child from the parent along it (tenet T17): `assertions` (an assertion about the parent is true of the child), `distributive` (only a statement or relation marked distributive on the group is true of each member), `context` (the parent's interactions overlapping the stay, as context, never fact) or `nothing`. A subject_statement_bindings row may carry `values`, a CLOSED list of the value terms the variable admits, each a {node, name} term that must be in the term registry (schemas/registry/did_v2_term_registry.json; tools/validate_v_eta.py R15, tools/check_term_registry.py R9); did2.build refuses a value outside it. An empty `values` list is legal and admits nothing yet: a value is added through review. A row whose statement value is data rather than a term (Gene Expression: the value is a body) says so with `term_valued: false` and carries no admissible set. (Jess Haley, 2026-10-21; recorded, not signed.)
